## Parent

turnkey-vnm

## What to build

A plain `tk test` just works. If the server isn't running, tk starts bazel-remote (pinned, by store path) detached. It listens on the fixed loopback port, with the per-user store under the platform cache dir. tk then passes the runner's `on` mode after `--` (spec §6).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A first `tk test` with no server running starts one and runs cached
- [ ] The store lives under the platform cache dir (turnkey/test-results/)
- [ ] A second `tk test` on unchanged Rust tests shows hits
- [ ] The mode flag never reaches the test and never enters the result key

## Blocked by

- turnkey-vnm.5
title: tk starts the local test result cache on demand
